change.describe: branch `pr-37634` of keycloak-37634 against c22f76867f595f0f7c327376a66a08dca01949e8 (merge-base c22f768)
change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut (wrong offsets and inverted condition)
findings.body: The encoded id is `<st 2><tt 2><gt 2>:<uuid>` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:78-81), so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`. This matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which straddles the token-type and grant chars. It also does `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, so a *matching* shortcut is rejected and a mismatching one is accepted. For `ofrtac:…` it compares `"ta"` to `"ac"`, which are unequal, so it returns true. The matcher therefore passes for essentially any id of the right shape, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` do not verify the grant type they claim to. Use `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)`. Also check `items[0].length() == 6` first. The `describeTo` text ("Not a Token ID with expected grant") reads like a negative expectation; say what is expected instead.

findings.title: Client credentials tokens are never tagged with their grant type
findings.body: `ClientCredentialsGrantType.process` builds the token through `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` and does not go through `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, which is where `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is set (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109). Nothing else sets the attribute on this `clientSessionCtx` (grep of `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` shows only refresh, pre-auth code, standard token exchange, ROPC and `createTokenResponse`). So `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` falls back to `na`, and client_credentials access tokens get ids like `trrtna:<uuid>` instead of `…cc`. The `cc` shortcut registered in ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory and the `trltcc` case in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest are never produced. Add `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` after line 122, as ROPC does at ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134. This file is not in the PR, so the change would have to be added. The same gap applies to the UMA permission grant (`pg`), which builds tokens in AuthorizationTokenService without setting the attribute.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check and never checks `rawTokenId`. A null raw id is accepted and `encodeTokenId` would produce `…:null`. Change the argument to `rawTokenId`.

findings.title: Unused import
findings.body: `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` is imported but not used. The attribute is set from `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` at line 237. Remove the import.

findings.title: assertEquals arguments are reversed and the session-context path is untested
findings.body: All `Assert.assertEquals(actual, expected)` calls pass the actual value first (lines 56-59, 68-71, 91-94, 102-105). JUnit prints failures with the roles swapped. The test also never covers `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` (transient/offline/online, lightweight, missing grant attribute → `na`), nor the malformed-id branches (length != 6, unknown session or token-type shortcut). Those branches are what decide whether a bad token id throws. A test of that path would also have shown the missing client_credentials attribute.

findings.title: Lightweight flag is read from session context client, not the token's client
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` calls `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, which reads `session.getContext().getClient()`. `initToken` is given the `client` the token is for. Is the context client always the same, for example in token exchange to a different target client, or in the admin evaluate and policy-evaluation callers that call `createClientAccessToken` (ClientScopeEvaluateResource, PolicyEvaluationService, KeycloakIdentity)? If it can differ, or be null, the `lt`/`rt` marker in the id could contradict the claims actually issued, or the call could NPE when no client is set in the context. Passing the client through, or reading it from `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient()`, would remove the dependency.

contracts.action: Every access token id is now generated as an encoded `<sessionType><tokenType><grant>:<uuid>` string instead of a plain UUID
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` in initToken. All callers of createClientAccessToken (grants, admin evaluate, policy evaluation, KeycloakIdentity, implicit/hybrid in OIDCLoginProtocol) go through this.
contracts.before_after: Before: random UUID. After: provider lookup, then context built from the client session context (session persistence state, lightweight flag, `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` attribute), then encoded. Flows that never set the attribute fall back to `na`, which encodeTokenId accepts (grantsToShortcuts contains `na`, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:79). Client credentials and UMA are among those flows and should have a concrete shortcut.
contracts.visible_effect: `jti` of access tokens and the `token_id` event detail change format. Client credentials tokens show `na` instead of `cc`.
contracts.failure_mode: If the provider is missing or the session type or grant is unknown, encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException and token issuance fails with a 500. Unknown grants are mapped to `na`, so the grant case is covered. Session type and token type are never UNKNOWN on this path.

contracts.action: Grant factory shortcut registry built at postInit and consulted when decoding or encoding
contracts.equivalent_path: Other factories (for example the Spi registry) read ProviderFactories lazily. This one snapshots them and refreshes on a miss.
contracts.before_after: Duplicate shortcuts are detected by comparing map sizes (a shared shortcut leaves the by-shortcut map smaller). Shortcuts in this PR are unique: ac, ci, cc, dg, pg, pc, rt, ro, te.
contracts.visible_effect: Startup fails with IllegalStateException if two grants share a shortcut.
contracts.failure_mode: Decoding an id with an unknown grant shortcut throws IllegalArgumentException. Callers that decode were not added in this PR.

summary: The change is mostly sound, but it has three defects. (1) The `isAccessTokenId` test matcher in AssertEvents is inverted and uses the wrong offsets, so it never checks the grant shortcut. (2) `ClientCredentialsGrantType` never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, so client_credentials tokens get `na` instead of `cc`. (3) `AccessTokenContext` null-checks `grantType` twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`. There is also a leftover unused import, weak assertion style in the unit test, and an open question about which client the lightweight flag is read from.
